title: Localization preserves quasi-excellence
statement: Let $R$ be a quasi-excellent commutative ring [def-exc-excellent-ring], and let $T\subseteq R$ be a multiplicative subset, meaning $1\in T$ and $st\in T$ whenever $s,t\in T$. Let $T^{-1}R$ be the localization of the $R$-module $R$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], endowed with its usual commutative ring structure $(r/s)(r^{\prime}/s^{\prime})=rr^{\prime}/ss^{\prime}$ and unit $1/1$. Then $T^{-1}R$ is quasi-excellent. The cases $T=\{1\}$ and $0\in T$ are allowed; no finite-generation assumption on $T$, universal catenarity, or ground field is required.

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, quasi-excellent alternative applied to the identity finite-type R-algebra R; arbitrary localization clause, lines 13372--13386.

proof.text: Put $A=T^{-1}R$. By [def-exc-excellent-ring], $R$ is Noetherian, a G-ring and J-2. The fraction construction [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] makes $R\to A$ a localization: denominators become units, every element is a fraction, and an element mapping to zero is killed by a denominator. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] gives that $A$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence; localization construction in Tag 00CM, section-localization.

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$ and put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. By clauses (1)--(3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], the canonical map $e:R_{\mathfrak p}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathfrak q}$ is an isomorphism carrying maximal ideal to maximal ideal. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-ring-equiv] to these maximal ideals. It gives $\widehat e:\widehat{R_{\mathfrak p}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat{A_{\mathfrak q}}$ with $\widehat e\circ\iota_R=\iota_A\circ e$. The map $\iota_R$ is regular by the G-ring hypothesis and [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-map-ring-equiv] to this commuting square: $\iota_A$ is regular. This holds for every $\mathfrak q$; together with Step 1 it proves that $A$ is a G-ring by [def-weil-pbc-g-ring].

source.place: Tag 07PV, proposition-finite-type-over-G-ring, proof first two sentences; the local-ring comparison is Algebra Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization, and the completion is the inverse limit of the corresponding quotients.

proof.text: Let $B$ be any finite type $A$-algebra. By [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra], $R\to A$ is essentially of finite type, using the identity finite type $R$-algebra $R$ and the set $T$; $A\to B$ is essentially of finite type using $B$ and the set $\{1\}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-composition]. The definition then provides a finite type $R$-algebra $C$, a multiplicative set $W\subseteq C$ and an $R$-algebra isomorphism $B\cong W^{-1}C$. Through this isomorphism regard $B$ as a localization of $C$ at $W$: the units, fractions and kernel identities are precisely those of $W^{-1}C$ carried by the isomorphism. Since $R$ is J-2, [def-exc-excellent-ring] gives an open regular locus $U\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}C$.

source.place: Tag 00QM, definition-essentially-finite-p-t; Tag 07DS, lemma-composition-essentially-of-finite-type; J-2 is More on Algebra Tag 07P7, definition-J.

proof.text: Let $h:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be contraction for the localization map of Step 3. It is continuous by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding]; this applies to the given localization presentation (equivalently identify $B$ with $W^{-1}C$). For every prime $\mathfrak b$ of $B$, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] gives $C_{h(\mathfrak b)}\cong B_{\mathfrak b}$. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ring-isomorphism] to this isomorphism and its inverse: $B_{\mathfrak b}$ is regular local if and only if $C_{h(\mathfrak b)}$ is. Consequently $\operatorname{Reg}(\operatorname{Spec}B)=h^{-1}(U)$, which is open. Since $B$ was an arbitrary finite type $A$-algebra, this is exactly the J-2 condition for $A$ in [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Tag 07QU, lemma-finite-type-over-excellent, omitted localization argument filled using Tag 07P7, definition-J, and Algebra Tag 00E3, lemma-spec-localization.

proof.text: Steps 1, 2 and 4 give all three conditions in [def-exc-excellent-ring], so $A$ is quasi-excellent. The arguments use arbitrary multiplicative subsets. If $0\in T$, the fraction relation [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] makes $A$ the zero ring, and every unital $A$-algebra is zero; the prime-indexed assertions in Steps 2 and 4 are then vacuous, while Step 1 still applies. Taking $T=\{1\}$ likewise requires no change. Universal catenarity, finite generation of $T$ and a ground field were never assumed.

Step 1: R to T^{-1}R satisfies (a)-(c) of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian. Step 3: R to A to B are both essentially of finite type (B=R with W=T, and B with W={1}); composition gives B iso W^{-1}C with C of finite type over R, and J-2 for R makes Reg(Spec C) open. Step 4: contraction is continuous by the spectrum-embedding leaf, C_{h(b)} is iso to B_b by clause (2), and of_ringEquiv in both directions gives Reg(B)=h^{-1}(U), which is open.
